summary: AI digital workers that execute procurement and supply-chain workflows for manufacturers.
editor_note: The stronger idea is procurement automation as an operating role rather than another dashboard: agents read contracts, invoices, email, ERP records and spreadsheets, then carry work from analysis through supplier action. The before-, during- and after-purchase loop covers value hunting, purchasing controls and recovery. Savings remain company reported, while permissions and human oversight inside critical systems are the central risk.
why_featured: $18M Series A for industrial AI workers
investors: Felicis Ventures, Sequoia Capital, The Westly Group

product_evidence.claim: Magentic's agents run procurement jobs across category analysis, purchasing controls, contract compliance and value recovery.
The agents connect contracts, ERP data, invoices, email and spreadsheets, and can prepare supplier actions while people retain control.

market_context.primary_user: Procurement and supply-chain teams at large manufacturers.
market_context.differentiation: Runs end-to-end procurement work inside existing systems instead of presenting a separate analytics dashboard.
market_context.why_now: Rising manufacturing demand and fragmented legacy procurement data increase the value of agents that can reason across existing systems.

risks.claim: Company-reported savings and adoption do not establish performance across customers, and write access across procurement systems requires careful permissions, auditability and human oversight.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment based on Magentic's official product and financing materials.
